restaurant_name: Chiang Mai Mother and Child Hospital
text:
I don't think many Japanese people give birth here, but my daughter did, so I'm recording it here. First, the hospital name is incorrect; officially it's the "Health Promotion Hospital." Since it specializes in obstetrics, gynecology, and pediatrics, "Mother and Child Hospital" is probably a more accurate name.

It seems to be a mid-range hospital in Chiang Mai; I didn't see any foreign patients. There were two doctors on duty at night and five during the day. It appears to be a major maternity hospital in the region; the facilities are quite old but sufficient, and there are many staff members.

The hospital has a policy against formula and disposable diapers; cloth diapers are provided. They strongly advocate breastfeeding, so it will be difficult for those who can't breastfeed. Of course, there are classes and other assistance available. A normal birth costs 21,000 THB according to the website.

My personal impression is that, compared to births in Japan, this hospital is very mother-centered. Because of breastfeeding, mothers and babies stay together unless there are special circumstances. If you expect hands-on assistance from the nurses, you might be disappointed.
